title: The four Session charts are computed over three different frame populations; the guiding chart includes frames the app rejected
what_happened: For seeded session 1 (12 light frames, 10 accepted + 2 rejected with rms 4.2", plus 4 darks) the four charts on one card report n=10 (Image quality), n=12 (Guiding performance), n=12 (Focus drift) and n=16 (Sensor temperature). The guiding headline therefore reads median 0.8 / p90 3.9 / range 0.5-4.2 and the 1" warning line is breached, when every accepted frame guided between 0.50" and 0.95". The temperature chart silently mixes in the 4 dark frames.
expected: All four charts on the session card should plot the same, stated population. HfrChart filters isAccepted; the other three do not, and none filters frameType==light. A p90 of 3.9" for a session whose accepted-frame p90 is 0.905" is a wrong number a user would act on (they would go hunting for a guiding fault that does not exist).
repro: Seed session 1 with 10 accepted lights (rms .50-.95), 2 rejected lights (rms 4.2, hfr 9.9, focuser 15100) and 4 darks (sensor_temp only). Restart. Analytics > Session > Reviewing > Night A - M31. Compare the n= counts in the four chart headers.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-analytics-08-s1.png - EXPOSURES 10/12 in the strip; chart headers n 10 / 12 / 12 / 16
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/analytics/widgets/session_chart.dart:375 (HfrChart filters isAccepted), :400 TemperatureChart, :425 GuidingRmsChart, :453 FocuserPositionChart (no filter at all)
proposed_fix: Filter one population in _SessionTab.chartGrid (accepted lights) and pass it to all four charts, or give every chart the same `.where((i)=>i.isAccepted && i.frameType==light)` predicate. If rejected frames are wanted, draw them as a distinct marker series and say so in the header.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced independently on my own profile (v-analytics, display :83). Analytics > Session > Night A - M31 renders exactly the claimed headers: Image quality n=10, Guiding performance median 0.8 / p90 3.9 / range 0.5-4.2 / n=12, Focus drift n=12, Sensor temperature n=16, beside a strip reading EXPOSURES 10/12. I recomputed the populations from sqlite rather than comparing two app readouts: session 1 holds 12 lights (10 accepted with guiding_rms_total 0.50..0.95; 2 rejected with hfr 9.9 / rms 4.2 / focuser 15100) plus 4 darks whose only non-null metric is sensor_temp -10.0. HFR therefore sees 10 rows, guiding and focuser 12, temperature 16. Guiding p90 over the accepted 10 is 0.905 by linear interpolation; over all 12 it is 3.875, which the UI rounds to the 3.9 shown - a 4.3x overstatement that also breaches the 1.0-arcsec warn line GuidingRmsChart draws. Every cited line is exact: session_chart.dart:375 is `.where((img) => img.hfr != null && img.isAccepted)`, :400 sensorTemp, :425 guidingRmsTotal, :453 focuserPosition, none filtering isAccepted or frameType. The mirror-image symptom also appears on session 5 (2 rejected lights): the HFR card says 'No HFR (px) recorded for these frames' while the other three report n=2 for those same frames. Note partial root-cause overlap with the darks-graded-Good finding (both stem from the Session tab never filtering frameType), but they are separate defects in separate files.

title: Exported FWHM is fabricated from HFR with the wrong factor (2.35x instead of 2x), overstating FWHM by 18%
what_happened: History > Night A - M31 > Export CSV wrote /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/Night A - M31_2026-08-01T14-40-26.csv with a populated "FWHM (px)" column - 4.70, 5.17, 5.64 - even though captured_images.fwhm is NULL for every one of those rows. The values are HFR * 2.35.
expected: For a Gaussian PSF the half-flux radius is 1.1774*sigma and FWHM = 2.3548*sigma, so FWHM = 2.00 * HFR. Multiplying HFR by 2.3548 treats HFR as sigma and inflates every reported FWHM by 17.7% (HFR 2.00 px -> 4.70" reported vs 4.00" true). Worse, the real `fwhm` column measured by the pipeline is ignored and overwritten by the derived number, and nothing in the CSV says the value is derived.
repro: Analytics > History > click Night A - M31 > click the spreadsheet icon; open the CSV. HFR column x 2.35 == FWHM column exactly.
evidence: /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/Night A - M31_2026-08-01T14-40-26.csv rows s1_000..s1_009; DB: select hfr,fwhm from captured_images where session_id=1 -> fwhm all NULL
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/session_export_service.dart:69-70 and :171; same factor in session_report_service.dart:301 (meanFwhm), capture_preview_loader.dart:180 (live capture FWHM readout), session_report.dart:36
proposed_fix: Use image.fwhm when present; otherwise derive FWHM = 2.0 * HFR and label the column "FWHM (px, derived from HFR)". Fix the constant in all four call sites - the live capture readout is showing the same inflated number during a run.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with my own fresh export rather than the reporter's file: History > Night A - M31 > fileSpreadsheet wrote 'Night A - M31_2026-08-02T12-05-18.csv' and every row's FWHM/HFR ratio is exactly 2.35 (2.00->4.70, 3.80->8.93, 9.90->23.27). `select count(*), count(fwhm) from captured_images where session_id=1` returns 16|0, so the column is fabricated, not read. session_export_service.dart:70 is verbatim `final fwhm = image.hfr != null ? image.hfr! * 2.35 : null;`, repeated at :171 for the JSON export, with the same factor at session_report_service.dart:301 and capture_preview_loader.dart:180. I checked the physics independently instead of accepting it: native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/stats.rs:672 documents and implements calculate_hfr_at_point as the true encircled-energy 50% half-flux RADIUS ('matches the NINA / SGP / PixInsight HFR convention'), and for a Gaussian that radius is sqrt(2 ln 2)*sigma = 1.1774*sigma while FWHM = 2.3548*sigma, so FWHM = 2.000*HFR and the 2.3548 factor treats a radius as a sigma - a 17.74% inflation, matching the claimed 17.7%. The 'measured column ignored' claim holds beyond this seed: imaging_service/persistence.dart:196 and imaging_records_repository.dart:420 do write a real fwhm and the exporter never reads it. Two nits: the cited evidence file ..._14-40-26.csv does not exist (the reporter's actual file is ..._14-39-48.csv), and the cited range 69-70 is really just line 70 (69 is the comment).

title: Insights invents a guiding baseline of 0.1 arcsec when there is no history, so every user with <=5 sessions is told their guiding degraded 7x
what_happened: The Science tab Insights panel showed 'Guiding degradation - Recent guiding RMS is 7.20x the historical baseline. Check balance, flexure, and backlash.' and 'Focus quality drift - Recent median HFR is elevated versus the longer-term baseline.' The five seeded sessions have avgGuidingRms 0.60/0.55/0.70/1.10/0.65 (mean 0.72) and there is NO older session at all - guiding never degraded, and the newest session (0.55) is the best of the five.
expected: With no baseline sessions, no baseline claim. The panel should stay silent (or say 'not enough history') instead of asserting a 7.2x regression and deducting 32 points from the equipment health score.
repro: Seed exactly 5 imaging_sessions with avg_guiding_rms 0.65/1.10/0.70/0.55/0.60 and avg_hfr 2.90/4.20/3.00/2.50/2.20. Restart. Analytics > Science > scroll to Insights.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-analytics-41.png. Arithmetic proof: baseline = recentSessions.skip(5).take(10) is EMPTY with 5 sessions, _mean([]) = 0.0, .clamp(0.1,100.0) = 0.1; mean recent guiding 3.60/5 = 0.72; 0.72/0.1 = 7.20 - exactly the number on screen.
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/equipment_health_service.dart:200 (baseline = skip(5).take(10)), :205-213 (.clamp(0.1,100.0) turns 'no data' into 0.1), :222 and :234 (the two triggers), _mean at :324
proposed_fix: Make the baselines nullable: if the baseline window is empty, skip both insights entirely and do not deduct score. The clamp exists to avoid divide-by-zero; the real fix is to not divide when there is nothing to divide by.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim: Analytics > Science > Insights shows 'Guiding degradation - Recent guiding RMS is 7.20x the historical baseline. Check balance, flexure, and backlash.' and 'Focus quality drift - Recent median HFR is elevated versus the longer-term baseline.' I recomputed from sqlite rather than trusting the panel: the five sessions carry avg_guiding_rms 0.65 / 1.10 / 0.70 / 0.55 / 0.60, mean 3.60/5 = 0.7200. equipment_health_service.dart:200 takes `baseline = recentSessions.skip(5).take(10)`, empty with five sessions; _mean (:324) returns 0.0 for an empty iterable and :207 clamps it to 0.1, giving 0.7200/0.1 = 7.20 exactly - matching the on-screen string to both decimals. The HFR branch is identical: recent mean 2.96 against a clamped 0.1 baseline at :213 always exceeds the 1.15x trigger. Both fire for ANY user with 1-5 sessions and deduct 18+14 = 32 points. All cited lines check out (200, 207/213, the two ifs immediately above the titles at 226/238, _mean at 324); the render site is science_analytics_tab.dart:387. One immaterial narrative slip: the newest session is Night E at 0.60, not 0.55 (that is Night D, second newest); the arithmetic is unaffected. P1 stands - the app asserts a 7x mount regression to every new user, and the fix is a no-baseline guard, not a threshold tweak.

title: Stored photometry for a past session is invisible: the light curve is filtered by the CURRENT global target selection, so reviewing any other night shows "has no data yet"
what_happened: Analytics > Science with 'Night D - V-Test' selected (120 frames, 480 photometry_measurements rows of which 120 are role='target', object_id='V-TEST', differential_magnitude sweeping -0.30..+0.30) renders 'Differential Photometry has no data yet', Period Analysis 'Need at least 10 photometry points (0 available)', no 'Export to AAVSO' button, and the Science guide ladder stuck on rung 2 'Track a star'.
expected: Reviewing a stored session should plot the photometry that session actually recorded. The DB holds a complete 120-point light curve for it.
repro: Proved by A/B in the running app. sessionLightCurveProvider filters photometry rows to objectId == activePhotometryTargetObjectIdProvider, which is `selection?.target?.objectId ?? 'target_primary'` - a single GLOBAL live selection, not a per-session lookup. I inserted 20 rows into session 5 identical in every way except object_id='target_primary'; after restart the Differential Photometry chart for Night E drew them (dMag axis -0.40..0.40, x 0s..1h35m) and the AAVSO export button appeared, while Night D's 120 real points stayed invisible.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/ra2-05.png (Night D: ladder stalled at 'Track a star', 'Pick a target'); tree for Night D shows 'Differential Photometry has no data yet' + 'Need at least 10 photometry points (0 available)'; tree for Night E after the target_primary insert shows a drawn 'Differential Photometry' chart with dMag ticks and 'Export to AAVSO'. sqlite: select object_id,role,count(*) from photometry_measurements group by 1,2 -> V-TEST|target|120 for session 4.
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/science_provider/session_products.dart:299-325 (sessionLightCurveProvider) and photometry_selection.dart:203-206 (activePhotometryTargetObjectIdProvider); write side uses selection.target!.objectId at services/science/science_processing_service/private_helpers.dart:169+
proposed_fix: For review mode, derive the object list from the session's own rows (select distinct object_id where role='target' and session_id=?) and offer a picker defaulting to the one with the most points; only fall back to the live selection for the session currently being captured.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced by driving the A/B myself. With 'Night D - V-Test' selected the Science tab renders 'Differential Photometry has no data yet' and 'Need at least 10 photometry points (0 available)', no Export to AAVSO, ladder stuck on rung 2 'Track a star' - while sqlite shows session 4 holds 480 photometry_measurements rows, 120 of them role='target' object_id='V-TEST' with a non-null differential_magnitude on every one. Changing only the session picker to 'Night E - M13' immediately draws a Differential Photometry chart with a dMag axis, surfaces 'Export to AAVSO', and Period Analysis reports 'analyze 80 data points' - because session 5's rows carry object_id='target_primary'. That object_id is the sole difference. I closed the loop from persisted state rather than inference: app_settings holds science.photometry.target_anchor = '' (empty), so photometry_selection.dart:205 `selection?.target?.objectId ?? 'target_primary'` yields the literal 'target_primary' and session_products.dart:313 filters `row.objectId == args.$2`. Both cited locations are exact (provider begins :299, filter :313; activePhotometryTargetObjectIdProvider :203-205). A stored night's light curve is unreachable and un-exportable unless the live selection happens to name the same object.

title: Optical Train Diagnostics grades a session with ZERO data as "A - Excellent" and states "tilt looks controlled" and "center and edge behavior look balanced"
what_happened: Analytics > Diagnostics > select 'Night D - V-Test'. The session has 120 plate-solved frames but zero psf_field_tiles and zero astrometric residual rows. The page renders 'Optical Health: A / Excellent', bars Tilt 0 and Collimation 0, a Tilt card badged 'Within range' with 'Score 0.0: tilt looks controlled for this session', and a Collimation card badged 'Centered' with 'Edge/center residual ratio: 0.0 - Center and edge behavior look balanced for this session'. The two panels immediately to the right of those verdicts read 'No PSF field tile data for this session. (0 tiles)' and 'No astrometric residual data for this session. (0 vectors)', and the Findings card reads 'No diagnostics data'.
expected: With no PSF tiles and no residual vectors the health grade, the tilt score and the collimation verdict are all undefined. They must render as '-' / 'Not measured' with the Findings card's own explanation, not as a green A. As shipped, a user who suspects tilt opens this tab, sees 'A / Excellent / tilt looks controlled' and stops investigating - the app has told them their optical train is healthy on the strength of no measurement at all.
repro: Analytics > Diagnostics > pick any session with no psf_field_tiles rows (a fresh install: every session). Compare the Optical Health grade with the '0 tiles' / '0 vectors' panels beside it.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/ra3-35-diagD.png; sqlite: select count(*) from psf_field_tiles where session_id=4 -> 0, and the same page reports 'A / Excellent'.
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/optical_train_diagnostics_service.dart (tilt/collimation scores default to 0.0 when the input lists are empty, and 0.0 is the BEST score, so 'no data' grades as perfect); rendered by packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/diagnostics/diagnostic_dump_screen.dart via the Analytics Diagnostics tab
location_wrong: The render citation is wrong. The Analytics Diagnostics tab renders DiagnosticsTabContent from packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/diagnostics/diagnostics_screen.dart (wired at analytics_screen.dart:241); the offending strings live in diagnostics_screen/health_summary_cards.dart:26 ('Optical Health'), :178 ('Within range'), :250 ('Score X: tilt looks controlled for this session.') and diagnostics_screen/optical_alignment_cards.dart:195 ('Edge/center residual ratio'), :208 ('Center and edge behavior look balanced for this session.'). The cited diagnostic_dump_screen.dart exists but contains no optical/tilt code at all - a fixer sent there finds nothing. The service citation (optical_train_diagnostics_service.dart) is correct.
proposed_fix: Make tiltScore/collimationScore nullable. When either input set is empty return null and render 'Not measured - needs N solved frames with PSF tiles', and suppress the letter grade entirely rather than defaulting it to A.
verdict_reasoning: Confirmed, with a caveat about which session I could reach. On Analytics > Diagnostics the panel for 'Night A - M31' renders in one view: 'Optical Health / A / Excellent', bars Tilt 0 and Collimation 0, a Tilt card badged 'Within range' reading 'Score 0.0: tilt looks controlled for this session.', a Collimation card badged 'Centered' reading 'Lower is better. Edge/center residual ratio: 0.0' and 'Center and edge behavior look balanced for this session.', a Findings card reading 'No diagnostics data', and beside them 'PSF Field Map / 0 tiles' and 'Astrometric Residuals / 0 vectors'. sqlite confirms zero psf_field_tiles rows for that session and an entirely empty astrometry_residual_vectors table. I traced the cause in source: the service's `if (psfTiles.isEmpty)` early return yields tiltScore 0 / collimationScore 0, and OpticalHealthScore.fromScores computes overall = 100 - (0*0.5 + 0*0.5) = 100, clearing the aThreshold of 90 - so 'not measured' scores identically to 'perfect'. Caveat: I could not render the finding's own session Night D - V-Test (120 frames); its diagnostics panel sat on loading skeletons for over 2.5 minutes with nothing in the log, so I used Night A, which satisfies the finding's own repro ('pick any session with no psf_field_tiles rows'). The session-4 DB facts it cites are nonetheless correct. P1 stands - this is the surface a user checks when they suspect tilt, and it returns a green A on zero evidence; the only mitigation is a small 'Need more solved frames to determine tilt direction' line that the grade and the two verdict sentences contradict.
